why: the 16-byte goal id as its own type. rcl carries it inside `rcl_action_goal_info_t` and rclcpp_action aliases it as `GoalUUID` (a `std::array`). Ours is a plain struct so it is copyable by value into caller storage with no allocator and no STL. Note our C++ grew `nros::GoalUUID` in phase-417 W4.b -- a standard-layout, trivially copyable value over the same 16 bytes; before that every C++ action signature passed a bare `uint8_t goal_id[16]`, which decays to a pointer.
